title: VoLUT: Efficient Volumetric streaming enhanced by LUT-based super-resolution
problem: 3D volumetric video streaming requires extremely high bandwidth; downsampling before transmission and upsampling via super-resolution at the receiver is needed, but existing 3D SR algorithms are too slow for real-time use on commodity mobile devices.
motivation: YuZu and similar neural 3D SR methods provide quality but require heavy per-point neural network inference that is too slow on mobile edge hardware. LUTs precompute the mapping from low-res to high-res point offsets offline, enabling fast lookup-table-based SR at inference time.
method: VoLUT has a two-stage SR pipeline. Stage 1 (dilated kNN interpolation): broader spatial context via dilated k-nearest neighbor search for initial upsampling; octree parallelism accelerates the kNN computation; neighbor relationships are reused across upsampling steps. Stage 2 (LUT refinement): coordinates of upsampled points are normalized to [0,1], quantized into b discrete bins per axis (bin=128 by default), and looked up in a precomputed 3D LUT that stores high-resolution position offsets (RF=4 receptive field, bin=128 yields 1.6GB LUT). The LUT is built offline from a trained NN model. MPC (Model Predictive Control)-based adaptive bitrate algorithm dynamically selects downsampling rate based on network conditions, streaming a continuous range of quality levels.
key_novelty: First system to run high-quality 3D point cloud super-resolution on commodity mobile devices at line-rate, using offline NN-to-LUT conversion with position encoding quantization and dilated kNN interpolation, combined with MPC-based continuous ABR streaming.
contributions: LUT-based 3D super-resolution: offline conversion of SR neural network to lookup table for fast mobile inference
Position encoding pipeline: normalize -> quantize to b bins -> LUT lookup of position offsets
Dilated kNN interpolation for broader spatial context in stage 1 upsampling
Octree-based parallel kNN with neighbor relationship reuse to reduce computation
MPC-based continuous ABR for volumetric video streaming adapting to bandwidth fluctuations
8.4x SR speedup over YuZu, 70% bandwidth reduction, 36.7% QoE improvement
hardware_target: Commodity mobile devices (receiver-side); server-side encoding; edge streaming
limitations: LUT size (1.6GB at RF=4, bin=128) may exceed mobile device storage for fine-grained configurations
LUT must be retrained/rebuilt if the content distribution shifts significantly
Dilated kNN still requires octree construction overhead at the receiver
